title: Fibrewise dense opens and relative rational maps
statement: Let $X,Y,S$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], with morphisms $f:X\to S$ and $g:Y\to S$. Fibres are scheme-theoretic base changes [def-pc-base-change]. An open $U\subseteq X$ is $S$-dense if its inverse image under $X_s\to X$ is dense for every $s\in S$. A fibrewise partial map from $f$ to $g$ consists of an $S$-dense open $U$ and an $S$-morphism $a:U\to Y$. Two such representatives $(U,a),(V,b)$ are equivalent when there is an $S$-dense open $B\subseteq U\cap V$ on which $a$ and $b$ agree. An $S$-rational map is the quotient by this relation. A fibrewise partial isomorphism consists of $S$-dense opens $U\subseteq X$, $H\subseteq Y$ and an $S$-isomorphism $e:U\simeq H$; its underlying partial map is $U\xrightarrow{e}H\hookrightarrow Y$. An $S$-rational map is $S$-birational if it is represented by such a fibrewise partial isomorphism.

source.place: BLR §2.5, printed pp.55–56 (PDF pp.61–62), definitions of S-dense open and S-rational map; the representative-isomorphism form used in §4.3 Proposition 5, printed pp.107–108.
